queue_items.claim: The strongest_rejected_alternative's sole ground is byte-false as to 25:17: the two verses do share an exact skeleton token, plus a shared root and a shared construction, and none of it is disclosed.
queue_items.grounds: The row states 'No merge with 25:15 or 25:17 was warranted; both are topically unrelated and share no skeleton token with this verse.' The 25:15 half is true (25:15 to 25:16 shows 0 shared exact skeleton tokens). The 25:17 half is false: 25:16 and 25:17 share the exact skeleton token pen, byte-identical in both verses, פֶּן (oshb:Prov.25.16) and פֶּן (oshb:Prov.25.17). Beyond the token they share the sin-bet-ayin root in the same slot, תִּ֝שְׂבָּעֶ֗נּוּ (oshb:Prov.25.16) against יִ֝שְׂבָּעֲךָ֗ (oshb:Prov.25.17), and the pen-plus-suffixed-yiqtol construction built on that root stands at exactly 4 verses book-wide (Prov.5.10, Prov.25.16, Prov.25.17, Prov.30.9; sweep: 4 verses), of which oshb:Prov.25.16 and oshb:Prov.25.17 are the ONLY adjacent pair. Both verses are admonitions against having too much of a thing. Nothing of this straddling device is disclosed here, while the 25:17 row does disclose the sin-bet-ayin root at the same seam. Load-bearing: this sentence is the entire stated warrant for rejecting the strongest rival, and a shared construction run is one of the owner gate's named cluster warrants for C5; the same run clusters oshb:Prov.25.11-Prov.25.12 on 1 shared content token plus adjacency, a thinner case than this one. Confidence high is correspondingly over-stated.
queue_items.proposed_change: PROPOSAL for adjudication, either arm: (a) replace the dead warrant with one that survives the true bytes, a replacement having to pass the test that killed the original, and disclose the pen and sin-bet-ayin construction straddling the 25:16 to 25:17 seam; or (b) respan Prov.25.16-Prov.25.17 as one proverb_cluster on the shared construction run, retiring the 25:17 atomic row. Dependent fields to re-open either way: observed_substrate_signals, device_notes, unit_type, confidence.

trigger_dispositions.grounds: The flagged sentence's universal word is 'only' inside 'eat only your fill', which paraphrases the verse's own אֱכֹ֣ל דַּיֶּ֑ךָּ (oshb:Prov.25.16), rendered by WEB as “Eat as much as is sufficient for you” (web:Prov.25.16). No count OBJECT, no corpus claim, so no sweep is owed. The row's one recurrence claim is digit-free but verifiable and re-derives TRUE: word-bound devash stands at 4 verses book-wide (Prov.16.24, Prov.24.13, Prov.25.16, Prov.25.27), so oshb:Prov.25.27 is indeed a second, non-adjacent honey-eating site. The row's real defects are the byte-false rival ground and the punctuation-sourced form label, carried by the findings below.

queue_items.claim: The ketiv/qere recurrence is counted inside a writer part and the digit 3 does not belong to the object the row names: that pair stands in 6 verses book-wide.
queue_items.grounds: The row's own site is byte-true: oshb:Prov.27.15 carries the inline unpointed ketiv מדונים before the pointed qere מִ֝דְיָנִ֗ים (both collate byte at Prov.27.15; pmarks_Prov.json kq records 1 note there, single witness). But 'in this part' scopes the recurrence count to the writer part, and the digit 3 does not belong to the object the row names. sweep.py --skel returns the ketiv skeleton in 6 verses book-wide (18:19, 21:19, 23:29, 25:24, 26:21, 27:15) and pmarks_Prov.json records a kq note at every one of them, so the ketiv/qere pair recurs at 6 verses, not 3; the pointed qere simply differs at three of them (מִדְיָנִ֣ים at oshb:Prov.21.19, מִדְיָנִ֨ים at oshb:Prov.23.29, and the waw-prefixed pair ומדונים וּ֝מִדְיָנִ֗ים at oshb:Prov.18.19). The digit 3 is reproducible only at an unnamed accent-identical tier, where the run מדונים מִ֝דְיָנִ֗ים is byte-identical at oshb:Prov.25.24, oshb:Prov.26.21 and oshb:Prov.27.15. Scoping the count to a writer part makes 3 come out right by coincidence and hides half the corpus-wide motif the row calls 'a recurring motif'.

queue_items.claim: The rival's rejection rests on an undigited genericity claim whose swept object is blended: the form actually shared across the seam is word-bound in exactly 2 verses book-wide, both of them this seam's own verses.
queue_items.grounds: הָ֝אָדָ֗ם (oshb:Prov.27.19) and הָ֝אָדָ֗ם (oshb:Prov.27.20) each collate byte at their own cited ref and are byte-identical to one another, and that definite form is word-bound in exactly 2 verses in the whole book (consonantal_index.json word-bound scan: Prov.27.19 and Prov.27.20, i.e. this seam's own two verses). The bare lexeme is a different object: 33 word-bound verses, and sweep.py --skel returns 44 verses / 46 token occurrences for the contiguous substring. observed_substrate_signals blends the two, calling it the shared skeleton token of the bare lexeme 'as' the definite form, and no digit appears anywhere in the row. Measured against the row's own comparanda the comparison inverts: זָ֭הָב is word-bound in 4 verses (11:22, 20:15, 25:11, 25:12), עָ֭צֵל in 12 verses plus וְ֝עָצֵ֗ל at 26:14, and הָג֣וֹ in 2 verses (25:4, 25:5) - so the form actually shared here is as narrow as the narrowest catchword the row calls narrower, and narrower than two of the three.
queue_items.proposed_change: Field repair: re-state the rejection with the object named and the digits given (definite form 2 word-bound verses book-wide, both at this seam; bare lexeme 33 word-bound verses / 44 substring verses), and re-derive the comparison, which inverts against two of the three cited catchwords. Routed onward, not adjudicated here: with the corrected digit the proverb_cluster rival at Prov.27.19-Prov.27.20 rests on a byte-grounded catchword of exactly the kind the cluster bar admits and must be re-weighed against the two similes' semantic independence; no span change is proposed by this auditor.

trigger_dispositions.grounds: 'the narrower catchwords adopted elsewhere in this part' is workflow register twice over: a writer-part range plus decision narration about other rows. queue_items.claim: The register map that carries the rival's rejection is byte-false at 30:4-5 and blends speaker-person with addressee-person.
queue_items.grounds: strongest_rejected_alternative rejects merging 30:7-9 into the preceding unit on '30:1-6's 3rd-person narration (30:1) and 1st-person confession before God (30:2-5)'. First-person forms stand only at oshb:Prov.30.2 (אָנֹכִ֣י, לִֽי) and oshb:Prov.30.3 (לָמַ֥דְתִּי, אֵדָֽע); oshb:Prov.30.4 closes second-person, כִּ֣י תֵדָֽע, and oshb:Prov.30.5 is third person throughout, מָגֵ֥ן ה֝֗וּא לַֽחֹסִ֥ים בּֽוֹ. The contrast also blends two categories: 30:7 is itself first-person speech (שָׁאַ֣לְתִּי, מִ֝מֶּ֗נִּי, אָמֽוּת), so what changes at the seam is the addressee - human at oshb:Prov.30.6 (בְּךָ֣) to God at oshb:Prov.30.7 (מֵאִתָּ֑ךְ) - not the speaker's person. Since the row names the register shift as 'the seam's real warrant', the rejection's stated ground is byte-false as written, though it is repairable and the seam itself survives on the numeral opener שְׁ֭תַּיִם.
queue_items.proposed_change: Field repair: state the register facts as the bytes have them - first-person confession at 30:2-3, third-person affirmation at 30:5, and an addressee shift from a human audience to God at the 30:6|30:7 seam inside continuous first-person speech - and let the numeral opener at oshb:Prov.30.7 carry the rejection. No span change: the seam stands.

queue_items.claim: Byte-true construction chains straddle both of the row's seams undisclosed, and the following verse is called unrelated against them.
queue_items.grounds: Opening edge: the vetitive particle heads oshb:Prov.30.6 (אַל תּ֥וֹסְףְּ), oshb:Prov.30.7 (אַל תִּמְנַ֥ע) and oshb:Prov.30.8 (אַל תִּֽתֶּן), the particle byte-identical at all three (collate byte at each ref). Closing edge: the lest-particle recurs at the skeleton tier - the forms differ in accent and one in prefix, so this is a skeleton-tier claim and not byte identity - at oshb:Prov.30.6 (פֶּן), twice at oshb:Prov.30.9 (פֶּ֥ן and וּפֶֽן) and again at oshb:Prov.30.10 (פֶּֽן), where the same vetitive also opens the verse (אַל תַּלְשֵׁ֣ן; the preposition אֶל in the same verse is the homograph and is not counted). Neither chain appears in boundary_rationale, observed_substrate_signals or device_notes, while the row asserts a clean register break at the opening edge and calls the following verse an 'unrelated servant/slander saying' - an overstatement against a shared vetitive opener and a shared lest-particle. The standing cross-seam rule makes a byte-true device straddling the row's own seam a disclosure obligation at both edges.
queue_items.proposed_change: Field repair: disclose both chains with their refs and argue the seams against them, since both survive (the numeral opener at oshb:Prov.30.7 and the petuchah-corroborated close at oshb:Prov.30.9); drop or qualify 'unrelated' for Prov.30.10. No span change proposed by this auditor, but the strengthened merge rival at Prov.30.1-Prov.30.9 is routed onward with the corrected disclosure.

trigger_dispositions.grounds: Well calibrated, and the stated reason is byte-checkable and honest. device_notes holds the band at medium_low because the seam rests on a register shift, with the petuchah only corroborating and the petition sitting inside the same first-person Agur material - and the bytes agree, since oshb:Prov.30.7 is itself first-person speech (שָׁאַ֣לְתִּי, מִ֝מֶּ֗נִּי, אָמֽוּת), exactly like oshb:Prov.30.2 and oshb:Prov.30.3. The mark claims are sound: pmarks_Prov.json records PE at Prov.30.6 and Prov.30.9, petuchah, single witness, correctly typed and disclosed at both, never conflated with the one SAMEKH at Prov.24.22 (check_marks GREEN, citation_sweep GREEN). The exclusivity digit is true at the object it names: the divine name is word-bound in 70 verses and 70 token occurrences book-wide and stands once in ch 30, at oshb:Prov.30.9 (מִ֥י יְה֫וָ֥ה, collate byte), while the contiguous-substring sweep returns 87 verses - so the row's 70 is the exact-token object the book's density figures use, not a mis-swept digit. The numeral opener שְׁ֭תַּיִם at oshb:Prov.30.7 is a genuine tier-1 signal the row could have leaned on harder, so the band understates rather than masks. The defects recorded below sit in the warrant's phrasing and in undisclosed straddling devices; neither makes medium_low the wrong band.

shipped_row.boundary_rationale: A new petition formula opens with the numeral שְׁ֭תַּיִם (oshb:Prov.30.7, "two things"), distinct in voice and grammar from the confession that precedes it -- the petuchah at oshb:Prov.30.6 (single-witness, disclosed) marks that seam. The petition is unpacked through a request to be free of falsehood and of both poverty and riches (30:8), reasoned in 30:9 with a rhetorical question naming the divine name directly, מִ֥י יְה֫וָ֥ה (oshb:Prov.30.9, "who is Yahweh"), the sole occurrence of that exact token in this chapter (sweep: 1 of 70 book-wide). The petuchah at oshb:Prov.30.9 (single-witness, disclosed) closes the petition before the unrelated servant/slander saying that follows.
shipped_row.strongest_rejected_alternative: Merging 30:7-9 into the preceding Agur unit was considered, since both are first-person material separated only by a non-driver petuchah at 30:6, but 30:7 shifts to a direct 2nd-person petition addressed to God, distinct from 30:1-6's 3rd-person narration (30:1) and 1st-person confession before God (30:2-5) plus 2nd-person warning to a human audience (30:6) -- the register shift, not the shared mark, is the seam's real warrant.

shipped_row.device_notes: The two-thing opening here anticipates the three/four formulas used later in the chapter's nature sayings, but unpacks two petitions rather than an itemized list of nouns -- texture distinguishing this saying's shape from the animal-list sayings, not a separate unit_type. Confidence is held at medium_low because the seam rests on a 1st-to-2nd-person register shift alone; the petuchah at 30:6 corroborates without independently marking a break at exactly this seam, and the petition sits inside the same 1st-person Agur material as the confession it follows.

prev_row.boundary_rationale: The unit opens on the header that begins Agur's collection, דִּבְרֵ֤י ... הַמַּ֫שָּׂ֥א (oshb:Prov.30.1, "the words of Agur ... the oracle"), and runs through a first-person meditation on the limits of human knowledge before God (30:2-4) into an affirmation that God's own word is tested and trustworthy (30:5) and a warning not to add to it, אַל תּ֥וֹסְףְּ עַל דְּבָרָ֑יו (oshb:Prov.30.6, "do not add to his words"). The skeleton דִּבְרֵ֤י occurs in 19 verses book-wide (sweep: 19), of which 9 are genuine construct-state "words of X" forms (1.6, 12.6, 18.4, 18.8, 22.12, 22.17, 26.22, 30.1, 31.1); the remaining 10 are pronominal-suffixed ("my/your/his words": 1.23, 4.4, 4.20, 23.8, 29.20, 30.6) or absolute-plural ("words": 10.19, 24.26, 26.6, 29.19) forms of the same root. Of the 19, the construct form opens the verse in 5 (sweep: 5 of 19, the verse-initial subset), and pairs with an oracle-word to form an actual collection header in only 2 of those 5 (sweep: 2 of 5) -- here and again at the Lemuel header. The petuchah recorded at oshb:Prov.30.6 (single-witness) corroborates this seam before the numbered petition that begins the next unit.
prev_row.strongest_rejected_alternative: Splitting the divrei/massa header (30:1) into its own row was considered, since it alone carries the disputed Ithiel-Ucal reading, but the first-person voice of 30:1 continues without interruption into the confession of 30:2, so the header stays inside the unit it opens.

prev_row.device_notes: Register is first-person confessional (30:2-5) framed by third-person narration about the speaker (30:1) and a second-person warning (30:6) -- parallelism class synthetic; descriptive texture, not the unit_type choice.
